harness.name: @intent/conformance-harness
harness.independence: Reference canonicalizer/hasher/merkle written from the written protocol rules only (ADR-005, arch doc §6.1); zero imports from the SUT in src/reference. The SUT is loaded exclusively via src/sut.ts from a frozen snapshot.

capture.note: Verbatim copy of Builder A's protocol-schema source at capture time. The harness imports ONLY this snapshot; the live tree is never loaded by tests.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: must criterion_id be unique within success_criteria?
freeze_blockers.rationale: No uniqueness constraint on criterion_id: two same-id criteria with different assertions are both schema-valid and mutually ambiguous for any verifier resolving criteria by id.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: must constraint_id be unique within constraints?

Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: which layer owns the total_amount == sum(outputs.amount) invariant (schema, policy, or settlement engine)?
freeze_blockers.rationale: Economic invariant total_amount == sum(outputs.amount) is not enforced anywhere in the delivered layer.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: what IS the canonical decimal form (and how are '-0'/'0.00'/'1.10' normalized)?
freeze_blockers.rationale: No canonical decimal form: '-0', '0.00', '1.10' are all accepted; the same economic value has multiple hashes across implementations.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: which layer owns Decision/Settlement cross-object binding (schema-time, verification-engine, or ledger)?
freeze_blockers.rationale: decision.intent_hash can be fabricated; no delivered API binds a decision to an existing Intent object.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: which layer owns Decision/Settlement cross-object binding (schema-time, verification-engine, or ledger)?
freeze_blockers.rationale: decision.evidence_root need not equal merkleRoot(bundle.artifact_hashes); the contradiction is representable.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: which layer owns Decision/Settlement cross-object binding (schema-time, verification-engine, or ledger)?
freeze_blockers.rationale: Settlement may reference a dangling decision_id and arbitrary proof_binding.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling 2026-09-17 (Issue #1 disposition): must be decided before G1 Freeze; cannot be deferred to a later layer. Question: must a SEALED bundle's merkle_root be verified against artifact_hashes at seal time?
freeze_blockers.rationale: A SEALED bundle may declare a merkle_root that does not match its artifact_hashes; only external recomputation detects the lie.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling R9 (PROOF TARGET BINDING), 2026-09-17: V1 proof_binding MUST bind at least intent_hash + milestone_id + milestone_revision + evidence_root + policy_hash. A proof must prove the result belongs to THIS specific milestone. Not deferrable to S1.
freeze_blockers.rationale: proof_binding is computed over (intent_hash, milestone_revision, evidence_root, policy_hash) ONLY; the binding function does not accept milestone_id. Two different milestones sharing those four values therefore share ONE proof binding: an old proof is replayable across proof targets. Demonstrated as a machine-reproducible collision by C-12-08.

summary.freeze_declaration: NONE — this report does not declare the schema frozen. Freeze authority belongs to the Commander. 5 FAIL findings, 33 UNKNOWN entries and 9 freeze blockers (Commander-ruled) must be dispositioned first.

attack_surfaces.title: NFC key-collision produces duplicate-key canonical JSON
attack_surfaces.detail: canonicalize({NFC 'é': 1, NFD 'e'+U+0301: 2}) emits '{"é":1,"é":2}' — invalid, ambiguous canonical text. A second implementation (or JSON.parse) collapses the keys, so the same canonical bytes can be re-read as a different object than the one that was hashed. The independent reference rejects this case.

attack_surfaces.title: -0 silently canonicalizes to 0 against the frozen spec text
attack_surfaces.detail: Spec header rule 4 says -0 is rejected; the implementation maps -0 -> 0. Two distinct JS values share one canonical form; a strict cross-language implementation following the written rule will refuse objects the TS implementation accepts (and hash differently on any value it does emit).

attack_surfaces.title: Schema admits values the canonicalizer rejects (unhashable-but-valid objects)
attack_surfaces.detail: Criterion.threshold uses z.number().int() (accepts 2^53, 1e308) while canonicalization requires safe integers; U64-as-string regex accepts 2^64 while u64be() throws. A schema-valid Intent/Settlement can exist that can never be sealed — parsers in other languages will disagree about whether the object is acceptable at all.

attack_surfaces.title: Timestamp format is shape-checked, not calendrically validated
attack_surfaces.detail: '2026-13-45T99:99:99.999Z' passes TimestampSchema despite being invalid RFC 3339. Cross-language timestamp parsers (strict RFC 3339) will reject objects the TS layer accepted, splitting the hash universe.

attack_surfaces.title: No canonical decimal form
attack_surfaces.detail: Amounts like '1.0' / '1.00' / '1' / '-0' are distinct canonical strings for the same economic value. Any component that normalizes decimals before hashing (or after) will disagree with one that does not. Settlement amounts are the highest-value instance.

attack_surfaces.title: Duplicate-key raw JSON collapses last-wins before canonicalization
attack_surfaces.detail: '{"a":1,"a":2}' and '{"a":2}' hash identically. Byte-level audit of evidence text diverges from hash-level identity; a malicious producer can include decoy keys that vanish in the hash.

attack_surfaces.title: Identifier uniqueness is unenforced (criterion_id, constraint_id, bundle_id reuse)
attack_surfaces.detail: Same-id different-content criteria are representable; the same bundle_id can seal two different artifact sets. Downstream resolution by id becomes attacker-choosable.

attack_surfaces.title: Cross-object references are free-floating
attack_surfaces.detail: decisions bind fabricated intent_hash/evidence_root; settlements bind dangling decision_id; bundles bind nonexistent runs. Nothing in the delivered layer enforces the §15.1 north-star chain (Receipt -> Settlement -> Decision -> Bundle -> Run -> Intent). The proof_binding construction is sound, but its INPUTS are unauthenticated at this layer.

attack_surfaces.title: SEALED bundle state does not imply a correct merkle_root
attack_surfaces.detail: The bundle invariant checks presence, not consistency: a SEALED bundle with a fabricated merkle_root parses. Detection requires every consumer to recompute merkleRoot(artifact_hashes) — cheap, but currently nothing mandates it.

attack_surfaces.title: Domain/version separation relies on 0x00 exclusion, not length prefixing
attack_surfaces.detail: hash_input = domain||0x00||version||0x00||canonical is injective only because (a) domain/version literals are frozen and 0x00-free and (b) canonical JSON escapes control characters. Any future domain string containing U+0000, or a non-JSON-escaping canonicalizer, breaks the separation. A length-prefixed design would not depend on both invariants.

attack_surfaces.title: Unicode strategy diverges from RFC 8785/JCS while claiming compatibility
attack_surfaces.detail: The spec header claims 'RFC 8785 / JCS compatible', but JCS does NOT normalize strings, while this protocol NFC-normalizes keys and values. A strict JCS implementation produces different canonical bytes (and different hashes) for any string not already in NFC. Additionally, lone surrogates and U+2028/2029 pass through as JSON-legal but JS-source-illegal text — a hazard for eval-adjacent consumers and some non-JS JSON libraries.

attack_surfaces.title: Delivered scope is a moving subset of the documented protocol
attack_surfaces.detail: Arch doc §6/§7 document 10+ object kinds and 6 state machines; the delivered snapshot contains 6 object kinds, a 2-state bundle lifecycle, and no transition engine, and it changed shape twice while this verification was running (events.js removed; Milestone/Plan/Run/Grant/Edge/Dispute dropped; content_hash renamed payload_hash; SubjectRef charset widened). Until Builder A declares a frozen revision, any conformance verdict is point-in-time only — which is why this harness pins a snapshot.

attack_surfaces.title: SubjectRef charset widened to include '@' without protocol review
attack_surfaces.detail: user:alice@evil is now a valid principal. Visual spoofing of email-like principal ids becomes representable in signed objects.

attack_surfaces.title: Economic invariants absent from every delivered layer
attack_surfaces.detail: total_amount != sum(outputs) parses; outputs are not bounded by any escrow notion; u64 nonce has no monotonicity. The A5/A7 principles (proof before payment, idempotent effects) currently rest entirely on undelivered engines.

attack_surfaces.title: proof_binding does not bind milestone_id (R9): cross-milestone proof replay
attack_surfaces.detail: proof_binding = H(intent_hash || milestone_revision || evidence_root || policy_hash) has no milestone_id in the preimage, and the delivered proofBinding() API cannot even receive one. Two distinct milestones sharing revision/intent/policy/evidence-root therefore share a single binding: a VALID decision for milestone A is a structurally valid proof for milestone B. Commander ruling R9 requires binding milestone_id in V1.
